newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tyndall issue to raise A$24.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tyndall issue to raise A$24.3 mln.

text.p: Investment group Tyndall Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it would raise A$24.30 million through a 1-for-10 rights issue at A$1.50 per share.
The company also announced a 1-for-10 bonus issue.
Earlier Tyndall, which is 52 percent owned by Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group Ltd, reported a 29.2 percent rise in net profit for the 1996 year to A$22.07 million.
It also set a 3.5 cents per share final dividend, bringing the total dividend for the year to 6.0 cents per share.
Earnings per share rose to 14.17 cents from 12.23 cents in 1995.

"In order to retire some debt, and to provide flexibility in developing further the core business activities of the group, the directors have decided to expand the capital base of Tyndall," Tyndall said.
Tyndall said the one for 10 bonus issue would be made on the expanded capital base after the rights issue.
Shares from both issues would rank for dividends in the 1997 year.
Tyndall's annual profit included profits from investment markets of A$8.369 million, up from A$5.747 million the previous year.
"Provided investment markets remain reasonably robust, the directors look forward to a satisfactory outcome in 1997," it said.
Tyndall later said it was confident of higher earnings in 1997.
Tyndall Australia's shares were up one cent at A$1.96 by 3.20 p.m. (0420 GMT).
